correctness.rationale: For each m>=2, the complete-graph two-token Laplacian is (4m-2)I-X^T X, the deleted matching contributes disjoint C4 Laplacians and m isolated states. Sign-character bases diagonalize the latter with multiplicities m+q,2q,q. The incidence map X has ranks m,m,0 on those three eigenspaces, with X X^T=(2m-2)I+11^T, giving all eigenpairs and multiplicities; their total dimension is m(2m-1), including boundary m=2. The only zero eigenvalue is simple, so matrix-tree theorem applies and gives the stated exact integer product. Independently built Python eigenspectra m=2..9 and exact determinant cases m=2..4, plus C++ finite-field nullities and determinants over two primes m=2..8, corroborate rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The 2-token graph of the standard cocktail-party family has nonuniform configuration degrees; its full unnormalized Laplacian spectrum is not equivalent to the well-known base-graph spectrum or just the known token spectral gap. The theorem classifies all eigenvalue multiplicities and computes spanning-tree complexity of a natural nonregular configuration graph for arbitrary m, with a tractable invariant-space explanation and direct relevance to finite-particle graph dynamics, graph-integrality examples, and exact tree complexity. No arbitrary slice or parameter was selected merely to obtain a small computation.
